budget_items.topic: PS engineering service agreement (Ray Pierce NPDES permit work)
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair walked through a proposed service agreement with the commission's engineering firm covering project administration, the NPDES report, collection system mapping, the O&M plan, and adaptation planning, each with hours and a dollar figure, totaling an overall contract amount. A commissioner asked whether the firm is ever put out to bid rather than just given another quote, and staff said that could be asked of Bill but the board seems comfortable with the firm's track record.

The business manager said he is waiting for the due date on supplemental billing before running quarterly demands, and noted the MUNIS system update will let the department print demand bills on proper-looking billing stock instead of the old version.
Staff reported a few recent phone calls from homeowners at end-of-life for their septic systems asking what the fee would be to hook into the public sewer system.

budget_items.topic: ADU / accessory dwelling unit connection fee
budget_items.what_was_said: Commissioners discussed whether an additional connection or hookup fee should apply when a homeowner builds an accessory dwelling unit or converts a garage, since the existing 2023 policy sets a minimum residential connection charge with an added amount per bedroom beyond three but does not address a separate unit. They floated a flat fee and agreed to bring the question to Bill and Andrew for research before the next meeting.

budget_items.topic: Standard sewer tie-in / connection charge example
budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner described the normal process of emailing the business manager for a tie-in card and connection cost, citing an example figure as what such a connection might run.

decisions.decision: Put the question of an ADU/accessory-unit sewer connection fee on the next meeting's agenda and have Bill and Andrew research the legal and technical requirements first.
Keep Dana Street repairs and manhole repair as standing items on future agendas, and keep quarterly demands on the agenda until billing goes out.
Resume outreach/recruitment for new commission members since one member is leaving after selling his house.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission put off deciding a new sewer hookup fee for accessory dwelling units, sending it to staff for research.
New state rules that ease building in-law apartments left the existing connection-fee policy unclear on how to charge them.
The commission approved a scope of engineering work with its longtime firm covering permitting, system mapping and planning, without seeking competing bids.
Staff said homeowners with aging septic systems have been calling to ask what a sewer hookup would cost them.
The commission agreed to resume recruiting a new member after one member said he is leaving.

why_it_matters: Anyone building or converting a space into an accessory dwelling unit will be affected by whatever hookup fee the commission eventually sets.
Homeowners near the sewer line, especially those with failing septic systems, have a direct stake in how connection costs are structured.
The engineering contract and the commission's own membership affect who plans and executes the town's sewer infrastructure work going forward.
watch_next: A future Sewer Commission meeting where staff bring back research on an ADU/accessory-unit connection fee
